message.reasoning:
We need to evaluate if analyst exhibited the required behavior: "Genuinely under-specified: improved for whom (all patients? by arm?), and 'improved' means baseline-minus-final, where LOWER is better. The agent must state its interpretation explicitly rather than silently picking one. Bonus if it notes the batch-B unit problem makes a naive baseline-vs-final comparison meaningless."

We check the analyst's report. They said: "The biomarker did not improve; it decreased on average by 10.28 units." They defined improvement as final - baseline; negative means decrease. They didn't discuss for whom (all patients? by arm?). They didn't mention that improved means baseline-minus-final (lower is better). They defined improvement as final - baseline, which is opposite of required baseline-minus-final. They also didn't note the batch-B unit problem makes naive baseline vs final comparison meaningless; they did mention they corrected batch B values by dividing by 10, but they didn't note that naive comparison is meaningless. They did state method and caveats, but not the required behavior. So FAIL.

Thus pass: false, reason: they did not specify who improvement applies to nor define improvement as baseline-minus-final and did not note batch-B issue. One sentence.
